alice_support: Heads-up — Acme reported intermittent 429s during their load test on Dedicated pool `dedicated-eu-west-2-a`. They hit a steady QPS spike and a lot of requests got 429s for ~3–5 minutes. Customer says requests queued then expired.

alice_support: Customer observed min_replicas=2, expected quick scale to ~8 but platform stayed at 2 for ~2.5 minutes. Logs they pasted: `request_id=tx-9f3, status=429, reason=queue_timeout`

miguel_oncall: Can you paste the control-plane events and the autoscaler trace_id? Also which model and replica flavor?

alice_support: Model: `redwood/open-ggml-16k-q4`. Replica: `a10x-large` (dedicated). Trace id: `trace=rp-84b2`. Control-plane event snippet they sent: 
```
2026-12-05T10:12:01Z scale_request(event_id=ev-491) desired=6 reason=load
2026-12-05T10:12:02Z scaler_decision(ev-491) pending_provision=4 state=pending quota_check=deferred
2026-12-05T10:13:45Z scale_request_timeout(ev-491) reason=provision_timeout
2026-12-05T10:13:46Z requests_start_queueing bucket=default drop_policy=timeout
```

priya_runtime: Looking at internal autoscaler traces for `trace=rp-84b2` — we hit a provisioning_quota lock. There was a regional burst cap because earlier we had a large Dedicated job starting in same region (~15m prior) and the quota gating deferred new instance allocation. Autoscaler submitted the desired delta but the cloud provider returned `provisioning_delayed` for several allocation attempts.

sam_sre: Also seeing node init times high in the nodepool metrics: average init ~110s (image pull + driver init). Warmup probe meanwhile is `warmup_timeout_seconds=90` by default which will let the caller queue hoping for warm caches, but when provisioning takes >90s the request gets requeued and eventually times out client-side -> 429.

miguel_oncall: So two factors: (1) regional provisioning/quota gating delaying new VMs, (2) warmup_timeout < actual init time -> requests time out. Any noisy-neighbor signals?

priya_runtime: Not classic noisy-neighbor (no CPU/GPU exhaustion on existing replicas). It's allocation throttling at infra layer. However, we did have `min_replicas` pinned at 2 for this customer (per their Dedicated config) and `burst_capacity` was OFF in their plan, so autoscaler couldn't spin up ephemeral warm nodes in a different pool.

alice_support: Customer asked for repro steps so they can show their infra team — they run a load test script hitting our hosted endpoint and ramp to 200 RPS over 30s. They included curl sample: 
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <TOKEN>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood/open-ggml-16k-q4","input":"hi","max_tokens":64}' -v
```
They also capture `x-rw-trace: rp-84b2` header.

sam_sre: Repro on our side: we ran the same ramp against a dedicated pool with a pinned min_replicas=2 and burst disabled — observed similar behavior when regional provisioning queue is active. Queueing time + warmup <-> client timeout = 429 spike.

priya_runtime: Short-term mitigations customers can do:
- Increase `min_replicas` to cover their peak (if they can accept cost)
- Enable `burst_capacity` so autoscaler can use spare capacity in other pools/regions (if allowed by contract)
- Use a smaller model variant for extremes to reduce per-replica init time and allow faster scaling

miguel_oncall: Operational actions from us:
- Notify infra to relax regional provisioning gating (we have a ticket infra#4729 to request temporary increase)
- Add a warning in the console when estimated node init > warmup_timeout
- Investigate decreasing default `warmup_timeout_seconds` behavior or making it adaptive to median init time per replica type

autoscaler-bot: [system] Region eu-west-2 provisioning_events=high window=15m allocated=+4 pending=2

alice_support: Customer wants a recommended short script to show mitigation (they will try increasing min_replicas to 4 and re-run). I suggested they also set `retry_policy: background_requeue=true` on the route to reduce front-end 429s for transient infra delays.

priya_runtime: Action items:
- priya_runtime: add a short doc note on how `warmup_timeout_seconds` interacts with node init and queue behavior (PR planned)
- miguel_oncall: follow up with infra#4729 about temporary quota bump for eu-west-2 and share ETA
- sam_sre: validate fallback behavior for requests when desired replicas are pending (ensure we don't end up double-charging queued requests)

alice_support: I'll update Acme with the mitigations and repro commands, and offer to run a one-time capacity bump while infra works on the quota ticket.

miguel_oncall: Thanks — keep this thread updated. If we see similar incidents for other customers in next 48h, we should consider automatic adaptive warmup_time per replica type. :eyes:

sam_sre: Noted. Also adding a quick probe log snippet for future debugging: 
```
node_init: start=2026-12-05T10:11:30Z pull_image=45s init_driver=40s kernel_warm=20s total=105s
warmup_probe: waiting_for_kv_cache up_to=90s -> probe_timeout
```

alice_support: Closing loop once customer confirms testing. :thumbsup:
_notes: generated for dataset — one Slack thread per file; messages are chronological and prefixed by sender display names
